transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, my regular doctor actually sent me here. My weight has dropped pretty low recently, and everyone seems to be making a big fuss about it. 

Honestly, I don't really see the problem. I'm a carpenter, and being this light... it just helps me keep up with the work in the shop. I don't get slowed down by carrying extra weight around, you know? But my doctor insisted I come see you, so here I am.
Have you been intentionally cutting back on how much you eat, or do you feel afraid of gaining weight?

I suppose I have been eating less, yes. On workshop days, I usually just have tea and... maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping for a real meal just feels unnecessary to me. It kind of throws off the control I’ve got over the day, you know? I prefer to just keep working.
When you imagine gaining some of that weight back, how would you feel about your body and how you look?

The thought of gaining it back... it really bothers me. Honestly, if I eat anything heavy, or even let myself have the kinds of foods we used to make for the holidays, I start worrying right away. I just get this fear that I’ll gain weight and lose the grip I’ve worked so hard to keep. I like the way my body is now because it shows I'm in control, and I don't want to lose that.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, so we can figure out where that puts you compared to what's expected for your body?

I'm about 5 foot 5, I think. As for my weight... well, I'm not exactly sure right now. I don't really keep track of the exact number, I just know I like where I'm at. My regular doctor weighed me, but I didn't really pay attention to what the scale said.
Have you ever had episodes where you eat a large amount of food and then try to get rid of it—by vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do that. I don't eat large amounts of food to begin with, so there's really nothing to get rid of. I just... stick to my routine and keep my eating very minimal. I don't make myself throw up or take anything like that.
Do you happen to remember the actual number on the scale from your last weigh-in, or could we weigh you now so we have an accurate current weight?

I suppose you can weigh me now if you really need to. I honestly don't remember the exact number from that last visit. I just know my regular doctor sent me here because my weight has dropped so low that everyone is making a big fuss over it. But, honestly, I don't see the issue. I feel like being this light helps me keep up with the work in the shop and not get slowed down.
Let's go ahead and step on the scale now so we can get your exact current weight - can you do that for me?

Alright. Just point me to where it is. I'll take my work boots off first, since they're pretty heavy from the shop and I know you want an exact number. Like I said, I don't really care what the scale says, but if you need to see it to move this appointment along, let's just get it over with.
Have your menstrual periods become irregular or stopped altogether since your weight has dropped?
Well, I'm 59, so... I haven't had a period in years anyway. That stopped a long time ago, way before any of this weight stuff started. So, no, it hasn't changed anything with that.
Now that you're on the scale, what does it show for your current weight?

Well, I don't have my reading glasses on, so I can't really make out the exact number from up here. The screen is facing your way anyway, so you can probably see it better than I can. What does it say?
I can see the display - your weight right now is 92 pounds. Given your height of 5'5", does that number surprise you, or does it match what you expected to see?

Ninety-two. Well, no, that doesn't really surprise me. I figured it was somewhere around there. 

My husband and the apprentices down at the shop keep saying I look too thin lately, but I just tell them I'm fine. Honestly, I think people are just confusing discipline with sickness. I work a physical job and I keep myself in shape. So, yeah, the number pretty much matches what I expected.
